item.title: Letter: Response to 'Scholars grapple with future of Israel studies in two-day conference'
item.description: To The Editor:I read The Herald's recent article "Scholars grapple with future of Israel studies in two-day conference" with interest. item.title: Letter: Response to 'Hegseth orders cancellation of attendance for troops in Brown graduate programs'
item.description: To the Editor:I remember the last divorce more than 50 years ago. item.description: On Friday, students, policy experts and industry professionals in finance and sustainability gathered on campus for the annual Future of Sustainable Investing Conference, a student-run event focused on the growing role of finance in addressing environmental challenges.FSIcon, the penultimate event of Brown's first-ever Climate Week, was entirely student-run and hosted in the Nelson Center for Entrepreneurship. item.title: R.I. community members, students protest Citizens Bank's alleged ties to organizations operating detention centers
item.description: On Saturday morning, approximately 50 community members gathered in front of Citizens Bank on Waterman Street to protest the company's alleged financial ties with the two largest private prison organizations in the United States, CoreCivic and the GEO Group.For years, the two companies have helped operate the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention centers.The rally was organized by Brown Rise Up, De-ICE Citizens Bank Coalition and a collection of local activist groups. item.title: 'Wicked' at PPAC was wickedly wonderful
item.description: Last week, the national touring cast of "Wicked" descended upon the Providence Performing Arts Center, where they will remain until March 22. The cast's dynamic performance complemented an already fantastic show, doing the classic justice.The 2003 musical is based on Gregory Maguire's 1995 novel, "Wicked: The Life and Times of the Wicked Witch of the West." item.title: Brown to offer hostile intruder training for students, faculty, employees
item.description: Brown will offer optional hostile intruder training to students, faculty and employees beginning next week, according to a Monday Today@Brown message.Students, faculty and employees can register online to attend the newly designed in-person or live virtual training sessions, which will be held between March 17 and April 9. item.title: The tropics may be getting even hotter than expected, Brown researchers find
item.description: The past 11 years have been the warmest on record. item.title: Deadline for R.I. coastal council appointments elapses without action

item.title: Benefit concert raises estimated $20,000 to support Brown Loves Providence
item.description: On Friday night, over 250 students and community members made their way to The Strand Ballroom and Theatre to attend a student-organized benefit concert in support of the Brown Loves Providence campaign.All proceeds from ticket sales - priced at $15 - would go to the initiative, according to event organizers. item.title: 'She Loves Me' brings vibrant romantic comedy to center stage
item.description: "She Loves Me," Brown Musical Forum's most recent show, has something for everyone to love.
